items.root_cause: The served feed's per_serving is a copy of v2-perserving cheapest_ps that reaches export-feed through recipe-costs.json, which top5-weekly writes AFTER check-ad-cycles has already run export-feed. Each day's first feed therefore ships the previous run's cheapest_ps. The feed only agrees with the hub (which reads v2 directly) when some later export happens to run the same day. On 2026-09-25 that lag was 30 slugs. Over the last 14 feed versions it ranged from 0 to 428.

root_fix.what: export-feed reads the per-serving cheapest from its owner, v2-perserving.json, instead of from top5-weekly's copy. The feed and the hub then read one file, whatever order the chain runs them in.
root_fix.exact_change: Add a pure function Get-TcFeedPerServing -RecipeCostRow $c -CheapestBySlug $map that returns [math]::Round($map[$slug],2) when the map holds the slug with a value > 0, and otherwise [double]$c.per_serving. That mirrors top5-weekly.ps1:34's own fallback. Before the recipes loop (export-feed.ps1:616), load meal-prep\pipeline\v2-perserving.json with Read-JsonFile into slug -> cheapest_ps. If it will not parse, print 'export-feed: WARNING - v2-perserving.json unreadable; per_serving falls back to recipe-costs.json (one run behind)' and use an empty map, never a refusal, because today's behaviour is the fallback. At :626 set per_serving = Get-TcFeedPerServing $c $v2map. Membership (which slugs appear, from recipe-costs.json), week_cost, sale_items, calories and servings are untouched. Considered and rejected: moving top5-weekly ahead of export-feed. top5-weekly is a reader step deliberately inside 'if (-not $guardsBlocked)' at check-ad-cycles.ps1:1941, and it also rotates the free dinners, so moving it would change what ships on a held board. Before landing, check with 'powershell -NoProfile -File ops\count-source-lifters.ps1 -Script grocery\export-feed.ps1' that no lifter needs the new function exported.

Membership, week_cost, sale_items stay recipe-costs' and one run behind; the membership lag is already printed by capture-run. The edit that converts it was prepared (prepare-article-price-edits.ps1) but could only land after the feed carried everyday_ps for free-chicken-alfredo. When that happened, the landing was left as a written sequence on a weekly-lane item with no run that executes it. So the page has read a stale, overstated price since the feed began carrying 2.00. The journal half had a separate cause (worktree-local ledger), which d05680d91 fixed.
items.root_fix_none_because: The landing IS the root fix for this post. prepare-article-price-edits' -Land replaces the literal with a feed-rendered span and refuses an edit that still carries a literal ('REFUSES an edit whose result still carries a literal the monitor would count'), so once it lands the price follows the feed with no later republish.

evidence: The backlog itself is drained and the count is corrected. design/ready-for-brad/propagate-backlog-2026-09-26.md measured 70, not 95 ('propagate: 70 dirty spec(s) of 587'), all real reader-visible changes since the 09-19 catalogue republish. 419535a9d fixed its three defects (-SlugsFile narrows; held/carriage refusals unstampable; planner drops of held recipes exit 0). 06305fc23 republished 54 of 67 and regenerated the Meal Plan Builder feed ('577 of 587 recipes ... 556 of 574 shared rows change cps'). d05680d91 republished the 13 drift-refused. The 3 held dangmyeon recipes are left dirty by design.

Today: propagate-recipes.ps1 -DryRun rc=0 'propagate: 33 dirty spec(s) of 587' (stamps file hash unchanged by the dry run). grocery/queue-depth.ps1 rc=0 'draining recipe-specs-awaiting-propagate 33 item(s) waiting, drained 30.1h ago (within 72h)'. That is new dirt since the 09-26 drain and inside the queue's own window, so it is not yet a defect.

The class question ('nothing pages when recipe changes sit unpublished') is NOT answered. A watcher has existed since 86f8d831c (2026-09-07): expected-automations.json declares recipe-specs-awaiting-propagate with max_age_hours 72, and health-heartbeat.ps1:934-935 raises 'QUEUE STUCK'. Its age is the LastWriteTime of meal-prep/pipeline/propagate-stamps.json (queue-depth.ps1:142-148). The stamps file had no commit from 3371c6df5 (09-19 06:18) to 06305fc23 (09-26 18:19), which is about 180h against a 72h bar. The heartbeat paged other classes on 09-23, 09-24 and 09-26 (alert-log 'MAIL DEFERRED Automation silent-death: TASK FAILED / TASK STALE'). Yet no queue item has EVER named QUEUE STUCK or awaiting-propagate (0 in grocery/triage-queue.json).

Ruled out so far: the bot's checkout sync does not rewrite unchanged tracked files (0 of 47 meal-prep/pipeline/*.ps1 last committed before 09-15 have an mtime after 09-19). Today's stamps mtime, 2026-09-27 07:00:05, is the sync bringing in d05680d91 (reflog 'capture-run sync: onto b1aa4df' at 07:00:05), which is a real drain arriving. propagate writes stamps outside a live run only under -Baseline (propagate-recipes.ps1:453-457). No heartbeat history survives (grocery/out/health-heartbeat-run.json holds only the last run), so what queue-depth printed on 09-22 to 09-26 cannot be read back.
items.root_cause: Unproven, parked at the effort ceiling. Proven: a watcher existed, the stamps went about 180h without a drain commit against a 72h bar, the heartbeat ran and paged other classes, and it never raised QUEUE STUCK. Not proven: which link failed. Either the stamps mtime was rewritten by something that is not a drain, or the heartbeat's queue branch did not reach the page. There is also a structural weakness regardless: the age is a file mtime, so ANY write to the stamps file (a -SlugsFile run that stamps 7 of 70, or a -Baseline) reads as a full drain and resets the clock while older specs keep waiting.
items.resolution_note: Backlog drained by others on 09-26 (70 measured, not 95; 54 plus 13 republished, 3 held left dirty by design; planner regenerated). Today 33 dirty, inside the 72h window. Class question still open: queue-depth plus the heartbeat should have raised QUEUE STUCK from about 09-22 and never did (0 queue items ever). Next probe: run health-heartbeat's queue branch against a sandbox copy with propagate-stamps.json's mtime set to 2026-09-19 06:18 and read whether a QUEUE STUCK issue reaches Send-AlertConditions (read ALERT-SIGNATURE at health-heartbeat.ps1:366-482 for dedup or suppression). Separately, age the queue by its OLDEST waiting spec rather than the stamps file mtime, so a partial drain cannot reset it.
